title: What is Polyline Annotation?
text: Marking long, thin objects in an image by placing points along them and joining the points into a line.

title: What is Polyline Annotation
text: To trace roads and lanes, to identify object paths, capture curved shapes
notes:
QUESTION 1: When the car is upside down in the air, can a person react fast enough? (No. Things happen in fractions of a second, so the car's computer must control the thrusters.)
QUESTION 2: Automated or autonomous? (Good discussion! The stunt is planned and practised in a closed area: the computer follows a plan and keeps the car balanced, which is mostly AUTOMATED. AUTONOMOUS would mean deciding by itself in new, busy places, like a city. The engineer says it cannot do that.)
QUESTION 3: Is it ready for the road? (No. Maybe production in 2028, and it must pass safety rules. Exciting videos are not the same as a finished product: always check the facts, as we learned in Part 4.)
INTERPRETER: thrusters = small jets that push the car; production = when the company starts making and selling it.
Source: NBC Nightly News report, supplied by the course organisers. Keep it for classroom use only.

title: What is Polygon Annotation?
text: What it is: Marking an object by clicking points around its edges.
How it works: Connected points form a shape that closely follows the object.
Why use it: Unlike a rectangle, it handles irregular or complex shapes.

title: Purpose of the project
text: The purpose is to identify damaged tools in the rail stations that could cause train accidents. This is a bounding box and polygon project.

title: Labeling criteria – pandrol_e-clip - normal
text: The yellow part is the pandrol_e-clip.
It looks like a pig tail.

title: Labeling criteria – pandrol_e-clip - abnormal
text: If the pandrol is not in its normal position, it is abnormal.
If the pandrol is around an existing location, such as the image on the left, please label the part itself.
If it’s away from its original position as shown in the image above, label the original position.

title: Labeling criteria – insulation_block- normal
text: The yellow part corresponds to the insulation block.
The example image above shows normal

title: Labeling criteria – insulation_block - abnormal
text: An abnormal insulation block includes broken or disconnected insulation blocks in different locations, or no insulation block at all.
Please check the examples above and the bounding box range.

title: Common Rules
text: Label with bounding box per object.
Annotations are tagged for each end of the object, and multiple annotations can overlap.
If part of the object is invisible or occluded, label the visible part only.
Label the object as far as it’s visible, regardless of its visible range.
